reviews.text: Adroitly balances moments of levity and epiphanies of pain; while also allowing long, uninterrupted takes to get under the viewers’ skin for a payoff that pierces, not only the body, but also the soul.
reviews.author: Paul Emmanuel Enicola

reviews.text: When preparing myself to see Drive My Car for the first time, I made sure to get to a cinema and allow myself to be captivated for the three-hour runtime.
reviews.author: Amy Smith

reviews.text: Drive My Car will not be for everyone, but for those willing, your patience will be rewarded in the purest form of empathy available for cinephiles this year.
reviews.author: Dave Giannini

reviews.text: Misaki and Kafuku are surrounded by an incredible ensemble of characters with the capacity to astonish, but the central relationship that develops in Drive My Car fuels Hamaguchi’s examination of how people choose to process long-internalized feelings.
reviews.author: Greg Carlson

reviews.text: Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s three-hour drama of Chekov and the difficulties of human connection did not miss connecting with audiences and critics.
reviews.author: Brian Susbielles

reviews.text: It has been said it is not about the destination, it’s the journey. Writer-Director Hamaguchi understands and is ever mindful of that. Drive My Car is a perfectly paced journey that allows Yusuke to reach his final destination right on time.
reviews.author: Dallas King

reviews.text: Could Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s Murakami adaption be his best yet?
reviews.author: Andrew Heskins

reviews.text: This film is complex and ambiguous, wordy, deliberate, character-driven and masterful. It earns every revelation, and it deserves every minute.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: I want to fall asleep while watching this film, I want to wake up and have it still be going, I want to simply exist with it at all times.
reviews.author: Mitchell Beaupre

reviews.text: Drive My Car may be a bit too patiently paced for some, but others will appreciate its skillfully subtle storytelling and astute analysis of grief - as well as the poignant performances from Hidetoshi Nishijima and Toko Miura.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: Drive My Car is intimate and detailed about every element of its on-screen voyage and its character studies, and also a road map to soulful, relatable truths.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: A deliberate film with an abundance of stories, some unusual, some disruptive, but all break conventional schemes and produce a decelerated sensation against the rhythm of our everyday lives. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juan José Beteta

reviews.text: "Drive My Car" is just as epic in its scope. Here, however, it's emotional scope, revealing the kind of feelings that may be small and personal at the start but widen to become vast and universal by the time the film reaches its powerful conclusion.
reviews.author: Tom O'Brien

reviews.text: Hamaguchi turns a monotonous dialogue-heavy narrative into an explosion that carries us through the rest of the film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: In its understated way, we're witnessing one of the most extraordinary and profound movies of recent cinema, in which a wordsmith filmmaker like Hamaguchi wins us over with the power of silence. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Elsa Fernández-Santos

reviews.text: A beautifully wrapped quiet work of art that hits you when you least expect it. It's a slow-burning arthouse vehicle about grief and love that unfolds over a three-hour run time.
reviews.author: Marriska Fernandes

reviews.text: One of the most delicate and beautiful works of our time... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro G. Calvo

reviews.text: Real cinema. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Victor Esquirol

reviews.text: Hamaguchi presents a film of amazing beauty that, with exquisite slowness, gains in detail and depth: in the style, yes, of Murakami, to make an automatic simile. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: In times when there is a particular insistence on the explosiveness of emotions, when lukewarmness is criticized as a lack of affective (or political) commitment, Drive my Car is not only a good film, but an important one.
reviews.author: Agustín Acevedo Kanopa

reviews.text: Drive My Car is a dramatic, artful showcase of human grief, love, and loss with exceptional acting that culminates in transcendence and freedom.
reviews.author: Sr. Rose Pacatte

reviews.text: Drive My Car looks at the nature of grief through the emotions of reserved characters, but conveys a world of healing that cannot be summed, only felt most ardently, most appreciatively.
reviews.author: Sukanya Verma

reviews.text: Pain and loss and grief and guilt are big emotions that the film manages to render small, which turns what should have been an emotionally engaging drama into a study in monotony.
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: The three hours of its intimate journey keep me buckled in my seat as, at a leisurely pace, it introduces his tragedy on wheels that examines loss, suffering, and self-acceptance in the endless pathways of human relationships. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Drive My Car is a mesmerising film that stays with you long afterwards. Its rhythm and pace enfolds the viewer: by the end you see how necessary and fitting that three-hour journey was and how much it encompassed.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: If the film feels like an enduring mystery by the end of its three-hour-long runtime, director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi creates the distinct impression that it’s only because people themselves often are.
reviews.author: Gayle Sequeira

reviews.text: Drive My Car is a film about grief, pain, guilt, shame, and the interface between art and life.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: The emotionally layered and very drawn-out Drive My Car won't appeal to people with short attention spans, but it's an immersive journey that memorably depicts the complexities of human lives. It's a three-hour movie where the last hour is the best hour.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: ...a largely (and distressingly) ineffective drama that mightve worked at half the length (but probably not).
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Following a similar direction as Chekhov, Drive My Car speeds past the ordinary into extraordinary terrain.
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: Drive My Car defies description or categorisation.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: Director Ryusuke Hamaguchi makes it easy to stay put. The film passes at a glide.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: Its Hamaguchis deeply human filmmaking that invests you deeply, and early on. You will care about these people, and youll want to see what happens.
reviews.author: Tony Stamp

reviews.text: We are a mixture of our experiences; mainly our traumas. Can art be cathartic for every experience? Or is there a limit to artistic expression before facing ourselves? Drive My Car encloses grief, love and soulmates spectacularly. Full review in Spanish
reviews.author: Victor Pineyro

reviews.text: The movie is powered by the understated performances of its two primary leads, both of whom employ a lot of stone-faced stoicism, their expressions concealing waves of grief with which neither has fully dealt.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: Ryusuke Hamaguchi's Drive My Car is a hauntingly beautiful drama that takes audiences on an unforgettable journey of love, loss and acceptance.
reviews.author: Sarah Bea Milner

reviews.text: This nearly three-hour production may be striving for something real or serious but does not achieve it. Drive My Car is a largely gloomy and tedious work that does not tell us much, if anything, about contemporary life.
reviews.author: Joanne Laurier

reviews.text: I wish it had been 30 to 45 minutes shorter and a little less obsessed with Chekhov, but it's fine.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: I really appreciated this film. It's very slow moving and you have to stick with it.
reviews.author: Tim Cogshell

reviews.text: It's talky without being snappy, languorous without being pleasurable.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: A film that is long (just under 3 hours long), winding and yet will capture your attention.
reviews.author: Carey-Ann Pawsey

reviews.text: It's representative of a kind of storytelling that Hollywood shies away from, fearful that if we don't write it on the wall in blood or neon six feet high people wont get it...Regardless of what it wins, it should be championed.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: Drive My Car shows a tender and melancholic way in which grief follows us around. Leading us to a wholly intimate and cathartic moment of acceptance where the reel and real dwell together and form newer meanings for those who can look through.
reviews.author: Shikhar Verma

reviews.text: If you can stick with the 3 hour run-time, you will be rewarded with a thoughtful film about avoiding the dark side of ourselves and others.  I wish the cinematography and editing were as artful as the writing.
reviews.author: Julia Swift

reviews.text: It’s a worthy entry in the great tradition of quiet, slow-paced Japanese dramas with an emphasis on character study.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: The movie takes its time building its narrative and defining its characters, and it requires patience to appreciate its many virtues.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: Drive My Car is a film of rare intimacy. It’s a quiet triumph, maybe the quietest.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: "The engine to the stirring momentum is Hamaguchis disarmingly gentle touch. It breathes with uncommon cinematic patience  a film of deep sighs  and the sensation only draws us in further into the folds."
reviews.author: David Lynch

reviews.text: In Drive My Car, Japanese director Rysuke Hamaguchi pressurizes the foundering emotional isolation in the Haruki Murakami story on which it is based to create an absorbing and discursive melodrama about communication, passivity, and regret.
reviews.author: Elissa Suh

reviews.text: The pieces Hamaguchi assembles don’t seem to add up, and yet when it’s over you may feel that the whole is much, much larger than the sum of the parts, in ways beyond the power to articulate.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Drive My Car slowly peels back the layers of peoples burdens, and the way they carry them in silence, as Hamaguchis signature lengthy dialogue scenes carefully chip away at his characters.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: Drive My Car uses its remarkably unhurried pace to shattering effect.
reviews.author: Calum Baker

reviews.text: Hamaguchi’s film shows that it will remain beautiful, and viewers will forget that they are not in the red Saab, and instead, they’re together, watching a movie.
reviews.author: Maxwell Rabb

reviews.text: Drive My Car's brilliance lies in its celebration of the dirtiness of life, and how our greatest triumphs exist in simply carrying on.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: A hypnotic, winding journey into the human heart and soul, sublimely well-executed with exceptional lead performances, a road movie deluxe that calls for an act of surrender
reviews.author: Jane Freebury

reviews.text: The logline doesn't do the film any favors, making it sound like a twisty thriller when really its a slow-burn drama exploring themes of grief in a way thats both epic and intimate, thanks to complex performances by Hidetoshi Nishijima and Tko Miura.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: A road picture with heart, soul and, as its various themes might suggest, a tribute to the swerves and straightaways of life on the thoroughfare ahead. Just please be patient and in no real hurry to get wherever it is you're going.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: It’s a well made, interesting film, but surely no masterpiece.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: A long movie, with much of its runtime confined to a car interior, might not sound compelling, but the script is both direct and subtle, the look is lucid but layered, and the performances underplayed but powerful.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: While Drive My Car counts as an easy win for multiculturalism, a male gaze persists throughout the film.
reviews.author: Li Lai

reviews.text: Everything about Drive My Car is so specific and purposeful.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: So Drive My Car is great  but is it three-hours great? Thats a decision left for each viewer. But I'll tell you this: For three hours, I was raptly paying attention, unable to guess where Hamaguchi was taking us next.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: An enthralling and introspective journey that takes us through the winding and mysterious roads of love and loss. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: An intimate character study and a captivating contemplation of love, grief, and human connection, it's one of the finest films of the season. Or any season.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: It’s mysterious, impenetrable, creeping forward on many fronts like a lava flow of ideas and nuance. It’s also throat-catchingly beautiful, as sad as a funeral, and wise in a way few films ever aspire to be.
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: It's an introspective film that emphasizes the importance of the road ahead instead of going around in the same circles every day, asking unanswerable questions of people who cannot respond.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: After you see Drive My Car, you will never look at snow, suspension bridges or stages the same way again. When you see the world through the searching eyes of director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi, there is no such thing as mere scenery.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: A miraculous movie that takes a solemn and mysterious anecdote about the unknowability of anyone outside of your own heart and transforms it into a beguiling film experience of incredible depth.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: Its emotional rewards are extraordinary in a way that describing what happens cannot truly convey.
reviews.author: Kayleigh Donaldson

reviews.text: Patient viewers will be rewarded with a deeply felt relationship movie that sees two characters working through their personal recoveries to find a path forward in life.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Its a beautifully crafted, moving, elegant and at times drily funny tale, superbly acted.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: Dont be intimidated by the length; director Ryusuke Hamaguchi paces the unfolding story in carefully judged emotional increments, using the awkward intimacy born of forced proximity to create an emotional landscape about loss, guilt and infidelity.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: I love the irony that a movie which such a simple, innocuous title could offer up such complexity.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: The length of the film is daunting, but it's also a thoroughly engrossing piece of art that's sexy and thoughtful.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: A work of slow cooking, of pause, of life in position to death, of our leadership, of the interpretation we carry out. Full review in Spanish
reviews.author: Guillem Martinez Oya

reviews.text: In Hamaguchi's films, men and women turn to art to redirect the unsatisfying narratives of their lives.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: Great films establish their own rhythm and seduce you into living on their time.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: Everything about the film is presented in plain terms and in plain sight, but Hamaguchi draws parallels and delivers reveals with so much gentle grace.
reviews.author: Thomas Caldwell

reviews.text: Not easy to sit through, but it never really drags. A penetrating look at our inner selves, but not for everyone.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: A thought-provoking ride that's enthralling in its quiet intensity. There's a lot of unpack here that leaves me ruminating even days after I watched it.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: Ryûsuke Hamaguchi's "Drive My Car" is an empathetic masterpiece that explores love, grief and the the porous line between performance and reality.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: To a person, the acting in "Drive My Car" is exceptional. Hamaguchi lets his film's rhythm play out carefully and quite beautifully.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: A slow and contemplative drama that takes way too much time setting up its third act, but the last hour is so good we forgive it for the first two.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: It's a somber, contemplative film with an uncanny rhythm.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Here's the best movie you never heard of, a flat-out masterpiece from Japan that's a frontrunner to win the foreign-film Oscar and maybe pull a 'Parasite" and compete for Best Picture. Why not? It's enthralling from first scene to last.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: What emerges is a powerful portrait of how two people can find solace in shared pain - and begin to work their way toward hope.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: The film has spellbinding moments.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: Drive My Car is obsessed with language, how the same phrase can be morphed and changed to fit any particular meaning, and how we use our words to conceal our feelings, not expose them.
reviews.author: Owen Gabbey

reviews.text: Ryûsuke Hamaguchi's film takes all kinds of unexpected swerves from the sparse text it's adapting. But it triumphs because it understands the weight of those little details.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: "Drive My Car" viewers need to be patient, but that patience is rewarded.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: Over the course of just under three hours, Hamaguchi reworks and expands a Haruki Murakami short story (it first ran in The New Yorker) into an intimate epic.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: Hamaguchi's long, measured, ultimately mesmerizing examination of the human soul.
reviews.author: Deborah Young

reviews.text: [This] kind of length has a way of embedding a sense of majestic scale into even the most simple, spare material.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: To me there was something unsatisfying about it...It was all warm feeling and cold technique. All I could think was: end it.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: Director Ryusuke Hamaguchi with co-writer Takamasa Oe have written a delicately tragic story about intersecting lives, drawing from the tradition of more than one culture.
reviews.author: Jana Monji

reviews.text: Much of Drive My Car comprises memorable scenes. Curiosity may be reason enough to see this award-winning film--at home. Be prepared, nevertheless, to fast forward (if watch on DVD or Blu-Ray) or get a snack from the kitchen.
reviews.author: Wendy Shreve

reviews.text: "Drive My Car" is an empathetic character study that requires real effort to watch, but patient viewers will be rewarded.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Hamaguchi more than compensates by eliciting heartfelt performances from Nishijima and Miura that leave you breathless.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: ...a daunting but ultimately rewarding watch.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: This is the kind of movie you want to hold in your heart for a little while after it's over, turning over its multiple meanings and sad secrets.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Digressive, literary, expansive in feeling, narrow in scope: with hardly a plot to burden it, Drive My Car is the filmed work this year that best offers up the pleasures of psychological-realist literature.
reviews.author: George Elkind

reviews.text: The drama unfolds during a production of Uncle Vanya. The lines spoken in play rehearsals often correspond to what is happening to the characters off stage in this clever screenplay by Ryûsuke Hamaguchi. The performances are very convincing.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: The film remains something all its own. It places us in the meditative mind of the middle-aged Tokyo stage actor and widower Kafuku, played with grace and kindness by Hidetoshi Nishijima...
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: Long, languid and lapidary in tone, 'Drive My Car' will be frustratingly slow to some, but to others almost transcendentally moving.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Ultimately, "Drive My Car" asks what's more important in an emotional life - objective truth or subjective belief? No easy answer. Just rebuild, repair and return, over and over until we're gone. Beautifully shot, stunningly acted & 2021's best film.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: Director and co-writer Ryusuke Hamaguchi and co-writer Takamasa Oe adapt a Haruki Murakami short story and create an impactful, nerve exposing rumination on love, the safety of our weaknesses, and the things that we're tethered to in loss.
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: Drive My Car shows people devastated by loss, allowing time to ripen those wounds and distort their understanding of love and purpose.
reviews.author: Estelle Tang

reviews.text: "Drive My Car" is quiet and stirring, anchored by exquisite performances byNishijima andMiura, and enriched with a sense of both longing and forward propulsion by directorHamaguchi.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: ...truly one of the best, most impactful films of the year.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: A dark horse Best Picture contender and a lock for a Best Foreign Film nod, Ryusuke Hamaguchi's intimate epic drama...
reviews.author: Samuel R. Murrian

reviews.text: Hamaguchi’s film is a meditative and intimate masterpiece. [...] the perfect interplay of elements ensures that Yusuke’s trajectory touches the spectator in profound ways and stirs the inner depths of his subject.
reviews.author: Pieter-Jan Van Haecke

reviews.text: Drive My Car is a slow moving and wonderful story, beautifully observed and executed, with love, loss and life at its core.
reviews.author: Paula Farmer

reviews.text: Director Ryusuke Hamaguchi uses his ample running time to help us understand his complex, guarded characters so we cannot help but feel happy when they find some measure of happiness
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: I'm reluctant to hand Hamaguchi Chekhovian laurels because his measured style feels like Chekhov when done poorly. Drive My Car is the opposite of lively.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: Adapting the Haruki Murakami short story to expound upon his own themes of performance and identity, cowriter (with Takamasa Oe)/director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi charts dual journeys of grief, each fueled by a different emotion...simply sublime.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Drive My Car certainly has admirable qualities. Those qualities, however, are too frequently pushed aside in favor of material that could easily have been trimmed with no discernible negative impact.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: A quietly moving, exquisitely made, intimate and emotionally unsparing drama about the communion between people, bonded by art or like-minded pain, things left unsaid and unanswerable questions.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: It has lots to say about love and its complexities, as well as regret and acceptance. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: These brilliant actors' physical travels parallel their psychological ones.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: ...Drive My Car suggests that, with the right combination of people riding together, you may be able to arrive, intact, somewhere special.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: Its three-hour running time flashes by.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Drive My Car chugs along with brilliant linearity-leaping across weeks and years to chronicle an artist's struggle to turn grief into inspiration.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: Its mystery propels it forward to a feeling of autonavigation, the sense that life keeps hurtling toward you even if you want to run from it. Better to have seen it without the distractions of a life at home and a second screen in reach.
reviews.author: Sean Fennessey

reviews.text: Drive My Car is required viewing for anyone who's ever been touched by art.
reviews.author: Cathy Brennan

reviews.text: A masterful, meditative achievement, this Japanese drama uses every bit of its three-hour running time to find subtle nuances and to sharply define characters by use of the empty spaces around them.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Movies can be driven as much by what's not said as by the words characters speak. That's true of Drive My Car, a complex, challenging movie from Japanese director Ryusuke Hamaguchi.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: A testament to art as something that's essential - rather than a frivolous activity for those who have money, 'taste,' or time.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Drive My Car won't be for everyone. It is well-acted and crafted, with enough narrative intrigue to hold one's attention.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Hamaguchi is adept in character study, his films unfolding as if they were novels, totally consuming.
reviews.author: Jenny Nulf

reviews.text: An incredibly subtle example of cinematic virtuosity and poetry.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Watching this film provided me with three of the most spellbinding hours that I spent watching movies this year.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: Moments bloom into radiant life.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: For a century and more, film directors have explored crosscurrents between art and life, and how one informs the other. Hamaguchi makes that exploration a fully humanized one.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Drive My Car is one of 2021's best films.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: The film firmly establishes its lonely and wounded characters, its melancholy tone, and its empathetic philosophy of the lost finding connections with each other.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Slow to build and with an assembly of characters who are all more complex than they seem on the surface, Drive My Car exemplifies Japan's growing body of literary cinema.
reviews.author: Jennie Kermode

reviews.text: With Drive My Car, Ryûsuke Hamaguchi crafts an emotional epic. It's a road movie through the soul and an odyssey well worth taking. You'll feel transformed by the journey's end.
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: Hidetoshi Nishijima is spectacular in this film.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: It's beautiful in every conceivable way.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: There is a deep richness to the film, especially in Yûsuke's emotional journey, and Hamaguchi does an excellent job of letting his characters' secrets unfold naturally.
reviews.author: G. Allen Johnson

reviews.text: It feels as expansive as the whole world.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: It feels like it moves at a clip even though, yes, it's at three hours. Very much worth a watch.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: The characters' relationships and internal drama is the key to Drive my Car. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: For many of us who may feel like we've stalled in our own great loss. Discovering Drive My Car may just give you the power to propel forward once more. A remarkable work that will stick with me for some time yet.
reviews.author: Darryl Griffiths

reviews.text: Ambitious and yet quietly confident, Hamaguchi's film feels an absolute treat.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: What begins as a shuttle between home and rehearsal spaces ends up taking the pair across Japan and on a journey through memory and loss.
reviews.author: Becca Voelcker

reviews.text: Hidetoshi Shinomiya's cinematography makes a trip to the dump look poetic. The entire ensemble is remarkable.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: Drive My Car is a rich and wonderfully soothing work, a film that only further confirms Hamaguchi as one of the finest directors working today.
reviews.author: Rory O'Connor

reviews.text: Drive My Car is an evocative display of our capacity for empathy, our need for change, and the catharsis of art and creation.
reviews.author: Allyson Johnson

reviews.text: Despite the three-hour duration, the film captivates with thought provoking parallels between art and life and reveals the characters' existential anguish with a quiet poignancy.
reviews.author: Diana Cheng

reviews.text: At the simplest of its many intricate levels, Ryûsuke Hamaguchi's "Drive My Car" is a masterpiece - haunting and true, melancholy and wise - inspired by another.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: What follows is a fascinating, multi-layered metaphor for power dynamics -- between driver and passenger, to be sure, but also between director and actor, play and performer, writer and text.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: It... takes a risk that doesn't quite work. But why fault a film for trying - especially when the initial results are so achingly good...
reviews.author: Ben Croll

reviews.text: It's an invigorating experience that never feels excessive in its run-time because we need each new dynamic to grow before its revelations can be earned.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Although it sometimes feels relegated to the slow lane, this character-driven Japanese drama rewards patient viewers with a multilayered study of redemption and reinvention through art.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: What it is can be summed up in a word that's often used loosely but fits the case here-a masterpiece, a mysteriously enthralling creation that keeps you guessing about where it's going, then reveals its essence with astonishing clarity.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: A drama of adult intimacy and meaning-of-life questions, Drive My Car is a refreshing adult road-movie examination of the unsolvable puzzle of other people's lives.
reviews.author: Liam Lacey

reviews.text: Drive My Car does not really come together until its final hour, but it accumulates an enormous charge by that point.
reviews.author: Steve Erickson

reviews.text: The movie is tender like a rainstorm: only in the aftermath, after you've allowed time for its ideas to settle, does its full picture become clear.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: "Drive My Car" sneaks up on you, lulling you in with visuals that are as straightforward as the narrative is complex.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: Drive My Car devastates and comforts through its vehicular poetry of the sorrow from which we run, the collisions that awaken us, and the healing gained from every bump in the road.
reviews.author: Carlos Aguilar

reviews.text: Slow and long though it may be, every moment in Drive My Car counts. Enjoy the ride.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: An emotionally compelling titan centered on loss, regret, betrayal, sex, and guilt
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Drive My Car effectively captures the double-edged nature of storytelling as a means of both processing and deflecting emotions...
reviews.author: Vikram Murthi

reviews.text: The impeccable Drive My Car cuts close to the bone of romantic and familial relationships and the fraught issue of trust and betrayal.
reviews.author: Graham Fuller

reviews.text: Patience is richly rewarded in the three-hour span of Ryusuke Hamaguchi's theatre-centered tale, adapted from a story by Haruki Murakami.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: Allow me to make a radical suggestion: The one film that demands to be seen on a big screen this year is a tiny little three-hour Japanese drama about grief, love and Chekhov.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: A meditative, profound and engrossing journey. Patient and emotionally mature audiences will be rewarded the most.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: This is a supremely confident piece of film-making from Ryûsuke Hamaguchi, albeit one that, at three hours long and with a rather Chekhov-heavy second half, will certainly require the right mindset.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: That very little happens in the way of narrative action speaks to how brilliantly Hamaguchi harnesses the emotions of his characters into compelling drama.
reviews.author: Christopher Machell

reviews.text: It's not for the impatient, but it's so precise and delicate, you won't notice the gear-changes.
reviews.author: Ian Freer

reviews.text: Few recent films have demanded to be seen in a cinema as much as this Japanese heartbreaker...
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: There is a certain Chekhovian staginess in Ryusuke Hamaguchi's film: characters open up to each other in extended speeches. If you can accept this, the movie rewards you with riches.
reviews.author: Edward Porter

reviews.text: Like a master craftsman gradually constructing his masterpiece. Drive My Car is an enthralling piece of cinematic wonderment.
reviews.author: Rob Aldam

reviews.text: Head-spinning in its psychological scope and dramatic sweep.
reviews.author: David Jenkins

reviews.text: Every cast member is superb. Every emotional beat resonates, and not a single facial expression feels false.
reviews.author: Ray Lobo

reviews.text: It's incredible and incredibly rewarding.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: Assured and enjoyable.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Hamaguchi gives the same importance to how what is said is said and how what is kept silent is kept silent. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel de Partearroyo

reviews.text: Like all of its characters, Mr. Hamaguchi has taken a yarn for a spin and transports it to his own.
reviews.author: Martin Tsai

reviews.text: Defying common notions of cinematic dynamism, the most powerful sequence takes place in a back seat, showing just two men talking. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fernanda Solórzano

reviews.text: A poised culmination of Hamaguchi's previous experimentations with form and style, this masterpiece marks the pinnacle of his career and cements his status as one of the most brilliant auteurs of contemporary world cinema.
reviews.author: Weiting Liu

reviews.text: Drive My Car isn't just splendid cinema, it's a bastion of possibility and wonder...
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: Thankfully the destination's worth the time... the entire journey is, gifting us an accumulation of moments compounding moments, an eventual heart-aching avalanche of miniature emotional stakes finding force though one another.
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: Somewhere, in the 3-hour long Drive My Car, there exists an excellent 2-hour long cut, but it is difficult to justify removing an entire third of the film out when the screenplay is this detailed and carefully written for each character.
reviews.author: Kevin L. Lee

reviews.text: Drive My Car is certainly a lengthy sit, but Ryusuke Hamaguchi's absorbing, epic three-hour drama finds a unique, affecting throughline to examine the crushing power of conflicted grief.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: The film more than justifies its three-hour running time, by developing relationships among its characters and audiences in a natural, unhurried pace.
reviews.author: Dustin Chang

reviews.text: A melancholy meditation of pain and performance that remains ever-enthralling.
reviews.author: Natalia Keogan

reviews.text: Even if one is aware that this film is as much a celebration of tone and mood as it is of plot, the play-within-a-play scenes go on even after the point is made.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: The structure is the first of [the film's] great virtues, but it's the sentimental restraint that elevates it. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jonay Armas

reviews.text: It's a superb piece of filmmaking, every bit as confounding and yet relatable as the human experience.
reviews.author: Sarah Kurchak

reviews.text: A perfect amalgamation of mood and meditation.
reviews.author: Shubhra Gupta

reviews.text: Drive My Car is a beautiful and mellow ride, although you'll need to stretch your legs after it ends.
reviews.author: Aparita Bhandari

reviews.text: Drive My Car works with such power because Hamaguchi never leaves his compassion at the door, instead opening it wide for it to overflow.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: Although Yusuke and Misaki eventually find some closure, the polyglot "Uncle Vanya" proves to be more engrossing.
reviews.author: James Hadfield

reviews.text: At two hours and 59 minutes, there is an endurance factor, but this is as patient and sensuous as movies get.
reviews.author: Max Maller

reviews.text: The prolific Hamaguchi... unveils his most complex endeavor yet with this tempest of fluctuating roles defined by formidable regrets and the difficulty of communicating.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: The film is ultimately about two people who saved each other from their own guilt, and these two actors embody that beautifully... a beguiling, slow-burning blast.
reviews.author: Zhuo-Ning Su

reviews.text: Hamaguchi might come at this idea from the opposite direction of his source material, but that disconnect is exactly what allows "Drive My Car" to reach its destination with such integrity.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Hamaguchi has imposed his own will on the Murakami story without complete justification, taking it much further than the short story cared to go.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Drive My Car's screenplay is an achievement to be experienced, an imaginative act of adaptation.
reviews.author: M.G. Mailloux

reviews.text: Despite what may initially seem to be a somewhat straightforward contemporary drama, Hamaguchi has crafted a rich, skilfully layered masterwork with flawless performances and a script that is a screenwriter's holy grail.
reviews.author: Gregory Ellwood

reviews.text: Hamaguchi has made a profoundly beautiful film about making peace with the role in front of you, and playing it with all your might.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: The film's three hours unfold in the most beautiful way possible in order to come together like a hug. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Miguel Muñoz Garnica

reviews.text: Holding his emotions in check quite superbly, [Nishijima] is a perfect vehicle for the film's subtle exploration of the debilitating forces that grief can unleash.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: The triumph of this extraordinary film is that it evokes this limbo half-life without itself feeling like purgatory, instead allowing us to gently observe without judgment and come away enriched.
reviews.author: Catherine Bray

reviews.text: Thinking about Drive My Car is necessarily reaching the gaze that does not individualize, that does not fragment, but unifies, that embraces a sensation more than an image. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge (JJ) Negrete

reviews.text: It is an engrossing and exalting experience.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Ryûsuki Hamaguchi's Chekhov-inspired Murakami adaptation is stellar yet frustratingly obtuse.
reviews.author: Adam Solomons

reviews.text: The numerous twists and turns between the characters end up leading to a unique reading of human complexity, finally embracing the strength and mastery of Chekhov's theater. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Àngel Quintana

reviews.text: [A] wise meditation on how the dead coexist with the living ... the first great film that Cannes 2021 has provided. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos F. Heredero

reviews.text: The performances are exceptional all around, but Nishijima and Miura really connect and make this three hour ride one worth taking.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: A sleek, streamlined slip of a thing that nonetheless, in the author's signature style, packs an awful lot into its lean sentences.
reviews.author: Guy Lodge

reviews.text: An absorbing, technically assured piece of work with poetic depths and novelistic ambitions.
reviews.author: Stephen Dalton

reviews.text: Not for all tastes, but attractive leads and mysterious interlocking narrative layers accompanied by a very pleasant score help make it seem shorter than its three-hour running time.
reviews.author: Lisa Nesselson

synopsis: Two years after his wife's unexpected death, Yusuke Kafuku (Hidetoshi Nishijima), a renowned stage actor and director, receives an offer to direct a production of Uncle Vanya at a theater festival in Hiroshima. There, he meets Misaki Watari (Toko Miura), a taciturn young woman assigned by the festival to chauffeur him in his beloved red Saab 900. As the production's premiere approaches, tensions mount amongst the cast and crew, not least between Yusuke and Koji Takatsuki, a handsome TV star who shares an unwelcome connection to Yusuke's late wife. Forced to confront painful truths raised from his past, Yusuke begins -- with the help of his driver -- to face the haunting mysteries his wife left behind. Adapted from Haruki Murakami's short story, Ryusuke Hamaguchi's Drive My Car is a haunting road movie traveling a path of love, loss, acceptance, and peace. Winner of three prizes at the 2021 Cannes Film Festival, including Best Screenplay.
